applies_why: No, because the judge text does not use a single verse's failure to state a link or its contrary; it uses the defender's dropped limb and absence of a live link.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse. It is not, if the judge names another verse or phrase that settles it.
why: The underdetermination is grounded on the dropped curse limb leaving no live link to contradict, not on a single verse not stating a link or its contrary, so the text does not breach K-S2.
